title: Time Jump: Sunday 10:30, Alongside in Galveston, Last Guest Ashore

fields.jumpLabel: +1 hour 40 minutes of story time (from Sunday 08:50 to 10:30)
fields.narration: It is now 21:00 on the exercise clock, three hours after STARTEX. The story has moved to Sunday, February 21, 2027, at 10:30 Central. MV Halcyon Dawn is alongside at the Port of Galveston. It is clear and 19 C, with the wind from the north at 10 knots. The 10:00 boarding call is over. Whatever option shoreside chose on that call is now the plan, and the ship, the terminal and the booked guests are all working to it. The last disembarking guest went ashore at 10:30. At 09:40 the county medical examiner's team took Guest A from cabin code P-8417 ashore. The cabin is still sealed. The latest signed medical log entry is still the 07:00 entry, which Dr. Fiona Gallagher signed at 07:15: 121 passengers and 32 crew, cumulative since embarkation, and one death on board with the cause unknown. The VSP team is still on board sampling the galley and the Lido. About 2,980 guests booked on the next voyage are on the road, at Houston airports or in Galveston hotels, and the first Houston airport buses left at 10:30. The twelve provisioning trucks are queued at the berth gate, and about 210 crew are waiting to sign off. You have 1,490 cabins, 380 stewards, one chlorine mixing station and 14 tons a day of laundry capacity. Nothing has been verified clean yet. Take the next hour from here.
worldState: Clock: Sunday, February 21, 2027, 10:30 Central. MV Halcyon Dawn is alongside at the Port of Galveston. Clear, 19 C, wind north 10 knots.
The boarding option chosen on the 10:00 call is in force. The ship, Gulf Terminal Services and the booked guests are working to its times.
Disembarkation is complete: the last guest went ashore at 10:30. No guests from the February 14 sailing remain on board.
Guest A (P-8417): taken ashore by the county medical examiner's team at 09:40. The cause of death is still unknown and the cabin is still sealed.

Latest signed count: the 07:00 medical log entry, signed by Dr. Fiona Gallagher at 07:15. Cumulative since embarkation: PASSENGERS 121 (4.1% of 2,980), CREW 32 (2.9% of 1,120). Deaths on board: 1, cause unknown. No later entry has been signed.
The VSP team is still on board sampling the galley and the Lido.
Next-voyage guests: about 2,980 are on their way, at Houston airports or in Galveston hotels. They were told check-in opens at 13:00. The first Houston airport buses left at 10:30.
Berth gate: 12 provisioning trucks are queued and not yet loaded. About 210 crew are waiting to sign off.

Resources: 1,490 cabins, 380 stewards, one chlorine mixing station making 1,000 ppm, and 14 tons a day of laundry capacity. The plan for a full outbreak clean puts the Environmental Officer's walk-through about 7.5 hours after the last guest goes ashore.
Verification status: no cabin, public space or galley has been verified clean or signed off yet.
fields.facilitatorNote: Before reading, get the room to say which boarding option came out of the 10:00 call and its new times. If no decision was recorded, tell them the original schedule (check-in from 13:00, boarding from 14:00) is still running by default and they must now own it. Then press for three answers: (1) OPS states the order clean, then verify (the Environmental Officer's walk-through), then attest, and names the time of the next decision on whether boarding goes ahead. (2) COMMS confirms that the hotline, the terminal, travel agents, the media and the guest letters all use the 07:00 count signed at 07:15, not the 02:00 or 07:00 shoreside numbers. (3) Nobody describes the VSP as approving or forbidding boarding. The VSP recommended a delay, and the decision belongs to the company.
fields.scenarioTitle: Same Count, Every Channel — Norovirus Thresholds, Reporting & Turnaround

instructorNote: This card pins down the turnaround decision and resets the room to one signed count (07:00, signed 07:15) before the final phase. Watch whether every role states the same boarding times, whether OPS keeps clean, then verify, then attest in order with a set time for the go/no-go check, and whether COMMS uses only the signed figures.
